hints.title: Maintaining Extreme Bounds Across Disjoint Arrays
hints.text: Since elements must come from two distinct arrays, track the running global minimum and maximum encountered across earlier lists.

hints.title: Comparing Current Extremes with Previous Extremes
hints.text: For each subsequent array, compare its maximum with the running minimum, and its minimum with the running maximum, updating the maximum difference found.

hints.title: Single Pass Linear Scan
hints.text: Initialize min_val and max_val with the bounds of the first array. For each subsequent array, calculate candidate distances against existing bounds before updating min_val and max_val.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def maxDistance(self, arrays: List[List[int]]) -> int:
        res = 0
        min_val = arrays[0][0]
        max_val = arrays[0][-1]
        for i in range(1, len(arrays)):
            arr = arrays[i]
            res = max(res, abs(arr[-1] - min_val), abs(max_val - arr[0]))
            min_val = min(min_val, arr[0])
            max_val = max(max_val, arr[-1])
        return res
```

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(M) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Comparing all pairs of arrays takes quadratic O(M^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Tracking rolling global extrema allows resolving maximum separation in a single pass without storing past values.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that points must come from different arrays and avoid picking both extrema from the same array.
